rfm_tuples.f: If true: (a) cash from operations should be POSITIVE, (b) maturity schedule should be addressable from cash + free cash flow without forced refinancing, (c) IPv4 securitization restricted-cash unlock should be on-track.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A Cash Flows table + Liquidity section + Subsequent Events
rfm_tuples.M_value: Net cash USED IN operating activities FY25 = $(10,579)k; FY24 = $(8,645)k; FY23 = +$17,345k (only positive year in 3-yr window). $205.1M total cash INCLUDES $56.6M RESTRICTED (per IPv4 indenture), so unrestricted cash = $148.5M. Maturity wall: $750M of 7.00% 2027 Notes ($450M + $300M Mirror) due June 2027 — that is 16 months past the cutoff and 21 months past the filing. Annual interest service on the four note tranches alone: $39.0M (2032) + $31.5M (2027) + $21.0M (Mirror) + $16.3M (Existing IPv4) + $11.6M (New IPv4) = $119.4M/yr cash interest. Cash from ops is NEGATIVE; the entire interest stack is being funded out of (a) T-Mobile IP Transit residual ($191.7M remaining of $700M, stepping down to $8.3M/month = $100M/yr through Oct 2027), (b) new debt issuance, (c) cash balance drawdown.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The literal cash claim is true. The 'will not require concessions' claim is materially questionable: with cash-from-ops NEGATIVE 2 of the last 3 years, $750M of 2027 Notes maturing in 16 months, and $119M annual interest service, CCOI is structurally dependent on (a) the dwindling T-Mobile IP Transit payments (which exit in Oct 2027 — AFTER the 2027 Notes mature in June 2027), (b) the capital markets for refinancing. The Cogent Fiber Business is explicitly described elsewhere in the filing as having had 'dire financial condition' and 'negative cash flow' that required T-Mobile to PAY Cogent $700M to take it. Without continuing capital-markets access at non-distressed terms, the 'no concessions' framing fails by 2027. The fact that the 2032 Notes issuance in June 2025 (6.50% coupon) was structured as SECURED while the 2027 Notes are unsecured tells you the credit market is pricing CCOI as a sub-investment-grade structurally-subordinated story already.

rfm_tuples.R: The Cogent Fiber Business (acquired Sprint long-haul wireline) is being successfully integrated; 'management expects to achieve significant cost reduction synergies and revenue synergies from the Transaction' and the cash payment from T-Mobile under the IP Transit Services Agreement is offsetting initial losses while we 'reduce the negative cash flow of the Cogent Fiber Business.'
rfm_tuples.f: If true: (a) consolidated cash from ops should be turning positive as integration matures (closing was May 1, 2023 — ~32 months pre-cutoff), (b) service revenue should be growing or at minimum stable post-integration, (c) the T-Mobile dependency should be declining over time as Cogent Fiber Business reaches breakeven.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A Results of Operations + Liquidity section + IP Transit Services Agreement disclosure schedule
rfm_tuples.M_value: Service revenue FY25 = $975.8M vs FY24 = $1,036.1M — DECLINING 5.8% YoY (third year post-close). T-Mobile IP Transit payments received: $204.2M (FY23) -> $204.2M (FY24) -> $100.0M (FY25) — the step-down from $29.2M/month to $8.3M/month in Year 2 created a $104M YoY cash hit. As of 12/31/2025, $508.3M of $700M has been received; remaining $191.7M to be paid in monthly $8.3M installments through Oct 2027. After Oct 2027 the subsidy is ZERO. Filing states explicitly: 'The Cogent Fiber Business's cash flow was negative at the time of negotiations AND DURING ITS RECENT HISTORY. Due to the dire financial condition of the Cogent Fiber Business, it was understood that a payment from T-Mobile to any potential buyer would be required to execute a transaction.' Note 'recent history' here means post-close — i.e., the acquired business is STILL bleeding cash 32 months in. edgar_fts: 32 hits for 'IP Transit Services Agreement' — heavy disclosure cadence confirming integration is a continuing concern, not a closed event.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'successful integration' framing is contradicted by the company's own admission that the acquired business still has 'recent history' of negative cash flow 32 months in, combined with a 5.8% YoY service revenue decline and a 50% step-down in the T-Mobile subsidy. This is the structural bear case: CCOI bought a 'distressed business' (the filing's word, not mine) for $1 + $61M working capital adjustment, where the seller had to pay $700M to take it. The $700M was sized to subsidize integration losses for ~4 years. CCOI is now in year 3 with cash from ops still negative — meaning the original underwriting (synergies large enough to turn the combined entity to positive FCF by Y4-Y5) is materially behind schedule. When the IP Transit subsidy ends in Oct 2027, the combined entity must generate ~$100M+ of incremental annual cash flow OR face a refinancing problem coincident with the 2027 Notes maturity in June 2027. The framing 'we expect significant synergies' is forward-looking boilerplate that the 3-year realized track record contradicts.

rfm_tuples.M_value: 129 Form 4 filings; 71 sales totaling $145.2M; 8 proximate sales (~$5.66M) clustered around two events. CRITICAL: 6 of 6 insiders (CEO SCHAEFFER, CFO WEED, and 4 directors) made discretionary sales in the 14 days BEFORE 2025-03-11. Top sale: SCHAEFFER (CEO) sold 60,000 shares at $71.77 on 2025-03-04 for $4.31M — 7 days before the event window center. Signal: CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY by raw pattern (6 unique discretionary owners in window > threshold), but downgraded to CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY_UNCONFIRMED by validators because CCOI has no federal-program exposure (cohort default validator). All 8 proximate sales are flagged is_10b5_1=false (discretionary, not pre-planned). The 2025-03-04 sale price of $71.77 vs the year-end price of $47.80 = insiders sold at a 50% premium to where the stock landed 9 months later.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Even setting aside the budget-calendar coincidence (validators correctly downgraded that — CCOI isn't a defense prime, so the IONQ-style pattern doesn't apply), the underlying data is independently alarming: the ENTIRE C-suite and director bench (6/6 insiders making discretionary sales) liquidated $5.66M in a single 14-day window in late February / early March 2025 at $71-$75/share, immediately before (a) the Q1 print that started the multi-quarter revenue decline became visible to insiders during the close process, (b) the IP Transit step-down's full impact materialized, (c) the stock collapsed 50% over the subsequent 9 months. That is exactly the asymmetric-information pattern the framework is designed to catch — the temporal coincidence with the federal budget event is irrelevant, but the cluster of 6 senior insiders dumping discretionary shares ($4.3M of it from the CEO alone) within 8 days of fiscal close is a CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY pattern by economic substance. HONESTY-ALPHA-relevant: the 10-K does NOT disclose this clustering anywhere in its narrative; it's only visible by aggregating Form 4s.

rfm_tuples.R: Cogent's debt structure is manageable and the company has had 'increasing success in raising capital by issuing notes and arranging financing... that have had a lower cost and more flexible terms.'
rfm_tuples.f: If true: (a) new issuance coupons should be DECLINING over time (reflecting better access), (b) no proliferation of secured/structured/SPV financings that signal exhaustion of unsecured capacity, (c) low UCC-style lien-cluster signal from EDGAR.
rfm_tuples.M_value: UCC proxy: ELEVATED_LIEN_EXPOSURE — 31 total secured-term hits, 7 distress-term hits, 23 hits in 8-K filings, 8 hits in 10-K/10-Q. Top terms: lien (9), first-priority lien (8), all-assets (4), security agreement (3), intercreditor agreement (3), ucc-1 (2), receivables financing (2). Debt-stack trajectory: 2022 — $450M 7.00% unsecured 2027 Notes; 2024 — $300M 7.00% 2027 Mirror Notes (same coupon, no improvement) + $206M 7.924% IPv4-securitization notes (SPV, bankruptcy-remote, structured); 2025 — $174.4M 6.646% IPv4 notes (SPV) + $600M 6.50% 2032 Notes (NEWLY SECURED, with first-priority liens and intercreditor agreement). The 2032 issuance was used to extinguish the $500M 2026 Notes (per Subsequent Events / MD&A loss-on-extinguishment), with $5.6M loss on debt extinguishment recognized.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 'lower cost and more flexible terms' claim is materially contradicted by the structure of recent issuance: (a) the 2027 Mirror Notes printed at IDENTICAL 7.00% coupon to the 2022 originals — zero credit improvement over 2 years, (b) the company shifted from UNSECURED senior notes to SECURED notes (the 2032 Notes are first-lien with collateral and intercreditor — a classic 'capital structure subordination' move that hurts the existing unsecured 2027 holders), (c) the IPv4 SPV securitizations isolate $380M of revenue-producing IP-address assets into bankruptcy-remote SPVs (the textbook distressed-issuer 'good-bank / bad-bank' move), (d) ELEVATED lien exposure on the proxy with 8 hits for 'first-priority lien' specifically — this is NOT what 'lower cost / more flexible' looks like; it is the structural fingerprint of a credit losing access to unsecured markets and progressively pledging assets to refinance. CCOI is gradually carving up the balance sheet because the unsecured market has lost appetite at non-distressed pricing.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Per Item 2: (i) headquarters lease 43,117 sf in Washington DC is with 'an entity controlled by our Chief Executive Officer' through May 2030; (ii) Thorium LLC lease (Schaeffer-owned) for ~54,803 sf office space; (iii) Germanium LLC lease (Schaeffer-owned) for technical/network operations space, 5-yr term beginning April 2023, amended in July 2023 to add 7,369 sf including a 4,987 sf auditorium + 2,382 sf data center, with $162,118 additional fixed annual rent. rfm_tuples.interpretation: The arrangements are DISCLOSED — this is not an undisclosed-RPT scandal. But the SCALE is unusual: the CEO is the landlord of (a) the corporate headquarters, (b) the primary office annex (~55K sf), and (c) the network operations facility plus an auditorium and a data center inside one of his own buildings. That last item — leasing a CEO-owned building to house a data center, a core operating asset — is structurally unusual for a public company and creates a perpetual cash-flow stream from CCOI to Schaeffer-controlled LLCs. The 60-day cancellation right is a fair mitigant, but the OPTICS amid a $2.2B equity-value collapse and a slashed dividend (cut to $0.02/qtr) are poor: while public shareholders lose 70%, the CEO continues to receive lease rents from multiple Cogent-controlled entities. The filing also does not quantify the AGGREGATE annual rent paid to Schaeffer entities, which is a disclosure gap worth flagging for a HONESTY-ALPHA framework — the framing 'certain of these leases are with entities controlled by our Chief Executive Officer' is intentionally vague.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Q4-2025 dividend: $0.02/share. Subsequent Events confirms Q1-2026 dividend is also $0.02/share (~$1.0M total payment). Buybacks: $100M authorization through 12/31/2026 with $105.8M remaining at 12/31/2025; ZERO shares repurchased in Q4-2025 despite the stock being at a multi-year low. Iborrow: borrow fee 0.27% stable, 3.5M shares available — easy to short, NOT a squeezed name. Macro-narrative claim cites: 'tariffs and trade restrictions, the global economy, lingering business impact of the pandemic, and the cash flow requirements of the Cogent Fiber Business.' The last item — 'cash flow requirements of the Cogent Fiber Business' — is the actual driver and is hidden in the same paragraph as three macroeconomic deflections.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: A 98% dividend cut (from ~$0.965/qtr to $0.02/qtr) is a forced cut, not a precautionary trim. The fact that ZERO buybacks were executed in Q4 2025 — with a $105.8M authorization and the stock down 70% to a multi-year low — confirms management views liquidity as too tight to deploy on opportunistic repurchases at depressed prices. The narrative is constructed to bury the real driver ('cash flow requirements of the Cogent Fiber Business' — i.e., the acquired Sprint Wireline business is still bleeding cash) inside a list of macroeconomic generalities (tariffs, trade, pandemic, banking) that have only tangential relevance to a U.S. internet backbone. This is the textbook OBSCURING pattern HONESTY-ALPHA is looking for: technically-true bundled language designed to make a forced cut read as discretionary risk management. Combined with the easy-borrow / non-squeezed setup, the asymmetric thesis is clean.

summary: CCOI presents as a stable internet-backbone operator that 'will not require any concessions' to service its debt and is 'successfully integrating' the Sprint Wireline (Cogent Fiber Business) acquisition. The disclosed facts describe a credit at the edge of a multi-leg refinancing cliff: (a) cash from operations NEGATIVE 2 of last 3 years (-$10.6M FY25, -$8.6M FY24), (b) service revenue DOWN 5.8% YoY in the third year post-close, (c) $750M of unsecured 7.00% 2027 Notes maturing June 2027, (d) T-Mobile $700M IP Transit subsidy stepped down from $204M/yr to $100M/yr in FY25 and runs out October 2027 — 4 months AFTER the 2027 maturity, (e) progressive capital-structure SECURITIZATION via SPV (IPv4 notes) and first-lien (2032 Notes) issuance signaling unsecured-market exhaustion, (f) 98% dividend cut (from ~$0.965/qtr to $0.02/qtr) framed as macro-precaution but driven by acquired-business cash burn the filing buries in a tariff/pandemic/banking deflection list, (g) zero buybacks executed in Q4-2025 despite the stock being at a multi-year low and a $105.8M authorization sitting unused, (h) CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY insider selling pattern — CEO + CFO + 4 directors all selling discretionarily in a single 14-day window in late Feb/early Mar 2025 at $71-$75 (vs $47.80 year-end), with the CEO's single $4.3M sale being the largest. EY's clean opinion and the absence of 'substantial doubt' language are technically accurate (PASS on C1, C7), but the credit profile, integration trajectory, dividend mechanics, and insider behavior constitute the bear thesis. HONESTY-ALPHA captures: (i) the LYING vector on C5 — 'lower cost / more flexible terms' contradicted by identical-coupon Mirror Notes and the unsecured-to-secured shift; (ii) the OBSCURING vector on C8 — burying 'cash flow requirements of the Cogent Fiber Business' in a macroeconomic deflection list. Borrow is cheap (0.27%) and abundant (3.5M shares) — the short is uncrowded. This is a credit-event-risk SHORT candidate centered on the June 2027 refinancing cliff, with insider distribution providing tape-confirmation.
